accuracy.evidence: Checked against NGSS 1-PS4-2 (objects in darkness can be seen only when illuminated) and 1-PS4-3 (objects placed in the path of a beam of light), the English national curriculum Year 3 Light statements (we need light to see; dark is the absence of light; shadows form when an opaque object blocks light from a light source; patterns in shadow size), and the Nuffield Primary SPACE research on children's ideas about light. The lab's shadow size uses the real similar-triangle ratio (screen distance over object distance from the torch).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the SPACE-documented ideas: shiny objects and the Moon are light sources (dark-room step, 'Shiny things bounce light'), shadows exist in total darkness (switch-off prediction and challenge tag 'always'), shadows sit on the same side as the light (first prediction), shadows keep the object's colour ('A shadow has no colour'), and moving closer to the light makes a smaller shadow (third prediction).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagshadow models one mechanism, a light source, a blocker and a screen: the beam is drawn as a cone, the shadow only appears when the teddy is inside it and the torch is on, and its size follows the distance ratio. flagsprout (plants need light) and the wave labs never block light with an object or project a silhouette. The shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers each idea by acting: no shadow until the teddy enters the beam, the shadow vanishes when the torch is tapped off, and dragging toward the torch visibly grows the silhouette while dragging toward the wall shrinks it. Matching a blank silhouette to a colourful toy shows that a shadow keeps shape but not colour.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: shadow 'Next to the torch', shadow 'stays on the wall' with the torch off, and 'Smaller' when the teddy moves close to the torch. Each is tested by the task right after it and the done message repeats the child's own guess.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with ten tagged wrong answers: shiny spoon or teddy as a light source, shadow toward the sun or on top of you, shadows in total darkness, red or yellow shadows, and smaller or vanished shadow near the torch. Each tag has its own correction naming the slip, e.g. 'The light is yellow, but the shadow is where the light is blocked.'

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK -0.7 against the family limit of 5.0 with sentences like 'No light, no shadow.' Adult text scores FK 9.2 against 10 and uses the precise terms light source, absence of light, opaque, transparent, block and reflect, plus the NGSS codes 1-PS4-2 and 1-PS4-3.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed. Kid paragraphs are things to try with a lamp, torch and hand; adult paragraphs carry the standards, the key vocabulary, the research-based mistakes and the lab outline. Overlap with the plants, waves and materials lessons is under the 12 percent limit.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360x640 in light and dark show the six dark-room objects in a 3 by 2 grid with readable labels, the torch, beam and screen side by side with the teddy clear of the instruction text, and the shadow silhouettes fitting the screen. Arrow and torch buttons wrap below the canvas; phone_sweep reported 0 findings.

accessibility.evidence: axe reported no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, with no console errors. Every drag or canvas tap has a button twin (the six object names, To torch, To wall, Up, Down, Torch on/off, cup/star/ball) and the canvas aria-label speaks each result, e.g. 'Torch off: no light to block, so the shadow is gone.'
